title: Tumor necrosis factor α stimulates taurine uptake and transporter gene expression in human intestinal Caco‐2 cells

sections.abstract: <jats:p>The effect of cytokines on the taurine uptake by human intestinal epithelial Caco‐2 cells was investigated. Among the various cytokines tested, tumor necrosis factor α (TNF‐α) markedly increased the taurine uptake by Caco‐2 cells, resulting in an increase in the intracellular taurine level. TNF‐α did not induce up‐regulation of the taurine uptake in hepatic HepG2, renal human embryo kidney 293, and macrophage‐like THP‐1 cells. The uptake of glycine,<jats:sc>L</jats:sc>‐leucine, and<jats:sc>L</jats:sc>‐glutamic acid by Caco‐2 cells was not affected by TNF‐α. A kinetic analysis of the taurine uptake by TNF‐α‐treated Caco‐2 cells suggests that this up‐regulation was associated with both an increase in the amount of the taurine transporter (TAUT) and an increase in its affinity. TNF‐α‐treated cells showed a higher mRNA level of the TAUT than did the control cells.</jats:p>
